title: Die himmlische Hochzeit
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 209. Text from Wikisource („Die himmlische Hochzeit (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly.
about: A poor peasant boy takes the pastor's sermon that whoever would enter heaven must always walk straight ahead quite literally, and does exactly that until he wanders into a strange city's church mid-service and refuses to leave, certain he has arrived in heaven. Mistaking the carved image of the Madonna and child for God himself, he begins sharing half his food with it every day; the image visibly grows plump on it, and one Sunday, after the pastor has quietly watched all this unfold, it invites the boy alone to the wedding — where, at his next communion, the boy falls down dead.

sentences.t: Es hörte einmal ein armer Bauernjunge in der Kirche wie der Pfarrer sprach „wer da will ins Himmelreich kommen, muß immer gerad aus gehen.“
sentences.l: A poor peasant boy once heard in the church how the pastor spoke, “whoever wants to come into the kingdom of heaven must always go straight ahead.”
sentences.i: A poor peasant boy once heard the pastor say in church, “whoever will come into the kingdom of heaven must always go straight ahead.”
sentences.n: “Bauernjunge” = Bauer (peasant) + Junge (boy), a plain compound. “wer da will …” has “da” as an untranslated particle here (roughly “whoever, in this matter, wants…”). “muß” is the 1857 spelling of muss. “gerad aus” = straight ahead, straight forward — the whole tale hangs on it, taken literally by the boy.

sentences.t: Da machte er sich auf, und gieng immer zu, immer gerade ohne abzuweichen, über Berg und Thal.
sentences.l: Then he set himself off, and went ever onward, ever straight without deviating, over hill and dale.
sentences.i: Then he set out, and walked on and on, always straight without turning aside, over hill and dale.
sentences.n: “machte er sich auf” is the reflexive separable aufmachen — to set out. “gieng immer zu” = went on and on (immer zu, an old fixed adverbial). “abweichen” = to deviate, turn aside; here as infinitive with zu (separable ab-). “Thal” is the 1857 spelling of Tal (valley); the -th- recurs throughout the edition.

sentences.t: Endlich führte ihn sein Weg in eine große Stadt, und mitten in die Kirche, wo eben Gottesdienst gehalten wurde.
sentences.l: Finally his way led him into a great city, and right into the church, where divine service was just being held.
sentences.i: At last his way led him into a great city, and right into the church, where a service was just being held.
sentences.n: “Gottesdienst” = Gott + Dienst, God’s service — a church service, worship. “eben” here is temporal — just now, just at that moment. “gehalten wurde” is a passive: was being held (as of a service).

sentences.t: Wie er nun all die Herrlichkeit sah, meinte er nun wäre er im Himmel angelangt, setzte sich hin und war von Herzen froh.
sentences.l: As he now saw all the splendour, he thought he had now arrived in heaven, sat himself down and was heartily glad.
sentences.i: When he saw all the splendour, he thought he had arrived in heaven; he sat down and was glad from the heart.
sentences.n: “wäre … angelangt” is reported subjunctive — his own thought, not the narrator’s claim. “setzte sich hin” is separable hinsetzen with reflexive sich — sat himself down. “von Herzen froh” — heartily glad, glad from the heart.

sentences.t: Als der Gottesdienst vorbei war und der Küster ihn hinausgehen hieß, antwortete er „nein, ich gehe nicht wieder hinaus, ich bin froh daß ich endlich im Himmel bin.“
sentences.l: When the service was over and the sexton told him to go out, he answered, “no, I am not going out again; I am glad that I am at last in heaven.”
sentences.i: When the service was over and the sexton told him to leave, he answered, “no, I am not going out again; I am glad that I am at last in heaven.”
sentences.n: “der Küster” is the sexton, the church attendant. “hinausgehen hieß” = told to go out (heißen + bare infinitive is a construction of ordering). “hinaus” is directional — out, away from the speaker (out of the church).

sentences.t: Da gieng der Küster zum Pfarrer und sagte ihm es wäre ein Kind in der Kirche, das wollte nicht wieder heraus, weil es glaubte es wäre im Himmelreich.
sentences.l: Then the sexton went to the pastor and told him there was a child in the church, who would not come out again, because he believed he was in the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.i: Then the sexton went to the pastor and told him there was a child in the church who would not come out again, because he thought he was in the kingdom of heaven.
sentences.n: The three verbs “wäre,” “wollte,” “wäre” are all reported subjunctive — the sexton’s speech laid inside the narrator’s frame. “heraus” is out toward the speaker (the pastor’s and sexton’s side); it pairs with the earlier “hinaus.”

sentences.t: Der Pfarrer sprach „wenn es das glaubt, so wollen wir es darin lassen.“
sentences.l: The pastor spoke, “if he believes that, then we want to leave him in it.”
sentences.i: The pastor said, “if he believes that, then let us leave him in it.”
sentences.n: “wollen wir” with a first-person plural is a light hortative — let us. “darin” (dar + in) = in it, therein. The pastor’s kindness sets the tone of the tale.

sentences.t: Darauf gieng er hin und fragte ob es auch Lust hätte zu arbeiten.
sentences.l: Thereupon he went over and asked whether he also had a mind to work.
sentences.i: Thereupon he went to him and asked whether he was willing to work.
sentences.n: “gieng … hin” is separable hingehen — went there, went over. “Lust haben zu” = to have a mind to, to be willing to. The subjunctive “hätte” marks the indirect question.

sentences.t: „Ja,“ antwortete der Kleine, ans Arbeiten wäre er gewöhnt, aber aus dem Himmel gienge er nicht wieder heraus.
sentences.l: “Yes,” answered the little one, to working he was accustomed, but out of heaven he would not go again.
sentences.i: “Yes,” answered the little one — he was used to work, but he would not go out of heaven again.
sentences.n: “an das Arbeiten gewöhnt sein” — to be used to (the) working; “an” takes the accusative in fixed uses like this. “gienge” (1857 spelling of ginge) is subjunctive II — reported and softening: he would not.

sentences.t: Nun blieb er in der Kirche, und als er sah wie die Leute zu dem Muttergottesbild mit dem Jesuskind, das aus Holz geschnitten war, kamen, knieten und beteten,
sentences.l: Now he stayed in the church, and when he saw how the people came, knelt and prayed to the Mother-of-God-image with the Christ child, which was carved out of wood,
sentences.i: So he stayed in the church, and when he saw how the people came, knelt and prayed before the image of the Mother of God with the Christ child, carved out of wood,
sentences.n: “Muttergottesbild” = Mother-of-God-image, a statue or painted image of the Virgin with the child. “Jesuskind” is another compound — Jesus + Kind, the child Jesus. “aus Holz geschnitten” = carved out of wood; a plain wooden statue, the ordinary furnishing of a village church. The clause hangs open on a comma — the boy’s thought completes it in the next unit.

sentences.t: dachte er „das ist der liebe Gott“ und sprach „hör einmal, lieber Gott, was bist du mager! gewis lassen dich die Leute hungern: ich will dir aber jeden Tag mein halbes Essen bringen.“
sentences.l: he thought, “that is the dear God,” and spoke, “listen here, dear God, how thin you are! surely the people are letting you go hungry: but I will bring you half of my food each day.”
sentences.i: he thought, “that is the dear God,” and said, “listen, dear God, how thin you are! Surely the people let you go hungry: but I will bring you half of my food every day.”
sentences.n: “der liebe Gott” — the dear God, a common German affectionate name for God, especially in children’s speech; the boy transfers it to the wooden Christ child of the statue. “hör einmal” — the flavouring particle einmal softens the imperative into “just listen.” “gewis” is the 1857 spelling of gewiss. “lassen … hungern” is the causative use of lassen — let/make go hungry. Read “du/dich/dir” throughout as English “you/you/you.”

sentences.t: Von nun an brachte er dem Bilde jeden Tag die Hälfte von seinem Essen,
sentences.l: From then on he brought to the image every day the half of his food,
sentences.i: From then on he brought the image half of his food every day,
sentences.n: “Von nun an” = from now on, from then on. “dem Bilde” carries the old dative -e on Bild, still felt in Grimm. “die Hälfte von” + dative is one German way of saying “half of.”

sentences.t: und das Bild fieng auch an die Speise zu genießen.
sentences.l: and the image began, too, to enjoy the food.
sentences.i: and the image, too, began to take in the food.
sentences.n: “fieng … an” is the 1857 spelling of fing an (anfangen, to begin; separable an-). “genießen” means both “to enjoy” and, in older use, “to partake of, to consume”; here the practical sense — the statue is taking the food.

sentences.t: Wie ein paar Wochen herum waren, merkten die Leute daß das Bild zunahm, dick und stark ward, und wunderten sich sehr.
sentences.l: When a couple of weeks were round, the people noticed that the image was gaining, becoming thick and strong, and wondered greatly.
sentences.i: When a couple of weeks had gone by, the people noticed that the image was gaining, growing plump and strong, and they wondered greatly.
sentences.n: “herum waren” = were round, i.e. had passed. “zunehmen” = to increase, to put on weight (of a person or, here, a statue); separable zu-. “ward” is again the archaic preterite of werden.

sentences.t: Der Pfarrer konnt es auch nicht begreifen, blieb in der Kirche und gieng dem Kleinen nach,
sentences.l: The pastor could not grasp it either, stayed in the church and went after the little one,
sentences.i: The pastor could not make sense of it either, stayed in the church and followed the little one,
sentences.n: “konnt” is a shortened konnte (past of können), common in Grimm before an accent. “nachgehen” + dative = to follow after; the separable nach- sits at the end.

sentences.t: da sah er wie der Knabe sein Brot mit der Mutter Gottes theilte und diese es auch annahm.
sentences.l: and there he saw how the boy shared his bread with the Mother of God, and she took it too.
sentences.i: and then he saw how the boy shared his bread with the Mother of God, and how she also took it.
sentences.n: “theilte” is the 1857 spelling of teilte (past of teilen, to share). “diese” = this one, feminine — the Mother of God (die Mutter). “annahm” is separable annehmen — to take, accept, receive (an- + nehmen, past 3rd sg.).

sentences.t: Nach einiger Zeit wurde der Knabe krank und kam acht Tage lang nicht aus dem Bett;
sentences.l: After some time the boy became ill and did not come out of bed for eight days;
sentences.i: After some time the boy fell ill and could not come out of bed for eight days;
sentences.n: “acht Tage lang” — the German idiom counts inclusively; a week and its two ends. “aus dem Bett kommen” = to get out of bed, literally to come out of the bed.

sentences.t: wie er aber wieder aufstehen konnte, war sein erstes daß er seine Speise der Mutter Gottes brachte.
sentences.l: but when he could get up again, his first was that he brought his food to the Mother of God.
sentences.i: but as soon as he could get up again, his first act was to bring his food to the Mother of God.
sentences.n: “sein erstes” — his first [thing], with the elided noun understood. “Speise” is food, nourishment (a plain older word, without any suggestion of a specific dish). “der Mutter Gottes brachte” — dative to whom, accusative what.

sentences.t: Der Pfarrer gieng ihm nach und hörte wie er sprach „lieber Gott, nimms nicht übel, daß ich dir so lange nichts gebracht habe: ich war aber krank und konnte nicht aufstehen.“
sentences.l: The pastor went after him and heard how he spoke, “dear God, do not take it amiss that I have brought you nothing for so long: I was ill, though, and could not get up.”
sentences.i: The pastor followed him and heard how he said, “dear God, do not take it amiss that I have brought you nothing for so long — I was ill, and could not get up.”
sentences.n: “nimms” = nimm es (imperative + enclitic es), common in Grimm’s speech. “übel nehmen” = to take amiss, take badly. “aufstehen” is separable auf- + stehen (to stand up, to get up).

sentences.t: Da antwortete ihm das Bild und sprach „ich habe deinen guten Willen gesehen, das ist mir genug; nächsten Sonntag sollst du mit mir auf die Hochzeit kommen.“
sentences.l: Then the image answered him and spoke, “I have seen your good will, that is enough for me; next Sunday you shall come to the wedding with me.”
sentences.i: Then the image answered him and said, “I have seen your good will, and that is enough for me; next Sunday you shall come with me to the wedding.”
sentences.n: “mir genug” — dative + genug: enough for me. “nächsten Sonntag” is the bare accusative-of-time (“next Sunday”). “Hochzeit” here is the heavenly wedding of the tale’s title — the reader knows already what is being invited to.

sentences.t: Der Knabe freute sich darüber und sagte es dem Pfarrer, der bat ihn hinzugehen und das Bild zu fragen ob er auch dürfte mitkommen.
sentences.l: The boy rejoiced over it and told it to the pastor, who asked him to go there and ask the image whether he too might come along.
sentences.i: The boy was glad of it and told the pastor, who asked him to go and ask the image whether he too might come along.
sentences.n: “sich freuen über” + accusative = to rejoice at, be glad of. “hinzugehen” = to go there (separable hin- with zu-infinitive). “mitkommen” is separable mit- + kommen — to come along, come too. “dürfte” is subjunctive II of dürfen — might, in the sense of being permitted.

sentences.t: „Nein,“ antwortete das Bild, „du allein.“
sentences.l: “No,” answered the image, “you alone.”
sentences.n: The reply is stripped to two words. The pastor is not to come.

sentences.t: Der Pfarrer wollte ihn erst vorbereiten und ihm das Abendmahl geben, das war der Knabe zufrieden;
sentences.l: The pastor wanted first to prepare him and to give him the Lord’s Supper, with that the boy was content;
sentences.i: The pastor wanted first to prepare him and give him Holy Communion; the boy was content with that;
sentences.n: “vorbereiten” = to prepare (separable vor-); here in the specific sense of preparing someone for Communion (confession, instruction). “Abendmahl” = the evening meal, and by long usage the Lord’s Supper, Holy Communion. “das war der Knabe zufrieden” has “das” as the topic — with that, the boy was content (old German construction).

sentences.t: und nächsten Sonntag, wie das Abendmahl an ihn kam, fiel er um, und war todt und war zur ewigen Hochzeit.
sentences.l: and on the next Sunday, as the Communion came to him, he fell over, and was dead, and was at the eternal wedding.
sentences.i: and on the next Sunday, as the Communion came round to him, he fell over, and was dead, and had gone to the eternal wedding.
sentences.n: “an ihn kam” — when the Communion’s turn reached him. “fiel er um” is separable umfallen — to fall over. “todt” is the 1857 spelling of tot (dead). “zur ewigen Hochzeit” — at (to) the eternal wedding; German zu can be “to” or “at” depending. The plainness is deliberate.

glossary.essen: das Essen — food, meal (nominalized infinitive; here of the boy’s daily meal shared with the image)
glossary.fragen: fragen — to ask (infinitive; here with zu, as “to ask the image”)
glossary.glaubt: glauben — believes (3rd sg. present; here of the boy who believes he is in heaven)
